thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: auth.login.failures spike — Okta userinfo returns 502 across multiple regions. paging oncall
Jordan: I'm on it. taking P (oncall)
Leo: seeing large volume of `502` from `https://okta.example.com/oauth2/v1/userinfo` in the API gateway logs
Maria: any customer impact numbers yet? which clusters are affected?
Aisha: support already has >10 tickets, customers get 'Unable to verify session' when opening console or trying to create new sessions
eng-sre: traced root to JWKS fetch failing: `GET /.well-known/jwks.json -> 502` from our token verifier in eu-west-1 and us-east-1
Jordan: can we apply a temporary mitigation: use cached JWKS while Okta recovers? need risk assessment
Leo: short-term cached JWKS is acceptable. token rotations within 24h could be missed but ok for immediate recovery. propose TTL=600s (10m)
Jordan: I'll do a canary toggle on `console-auth` route in eu-west-1 with jwks_cache_ttl=600s
deploy-bot: rollout started: console-auth jwks_cache_ttl -> 600s ; canary 10% -> 50%
Aisha: preparing support note: "Intermittent login failures in EU/US — engineering investigating (Okta API 502)." Drafting targeted replies for enterprise tenants
Maria: which tenants show most errors? need to prioritize outbound comms
eng-sre: quick query: `SELECT tenant_id, count(*) FROM auth_errors WHERE err_type='JWKS_FETCH_502' GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 10;` -> tenant-42, tenant-7, tenant-88 top of list
Jordan: noted. assigning tenant-42 to Aisha for direct outreach. handing incident lead to Leo in 30m (handoff plan)
Leo: ack. I'll take lead after handoff. digging into Okta status now
Leo: Okta status page shows 'Degraded' for Authorization services in EU and US regions (incident posted 5m ago) — https://status.okta.com/incidents/xxxx
support-bot: support ticket #12345 created for tenant-42, assigned to Aisha
Aisha: sending targeted note to tenant-42: workaround is to retry login; if persists, use admin magic-link flow we've shared previously. Escalate to account manager if they report enterprise impact
Maria: quick customer impact summary for status page: approx 3% DAU unable to sign in between 21:05-21:20 UTC, affecting console and some API auths, no data loss reported
eng-sre: metrics in canary: auth failures dropped from 5.3% -> 1.2% in the region with cached JWKS
Jordan: expansion plan: increase jwks_cache_ttl canary to 100% across regions (exclude legacy mobile route) in 5m if metrics hold
deploy-bot: rollout to 100% complete for console-auth (jwks_cache_ttl=600s). Monitoring enabled
Leo: recommend adding a policy: accept tokens validated with cached keys for login flows, but require revalidation for high-privilege actions (console admin APIs)
Jordan: filing incident ticket INC-202 with timeline, mitigation, and owners
incident-bot: Incident declared SEV2 at 2156789012. Primary oncall: Jordan. Handoff planned at 2156789210 to Leo
Jordan: handing off to @Leo now. leaving runbook notes and executed queries in incident doc.
Leo: taking over incident lead. next steps: keep Okta engaged for root cause, track for token rotation edge cases, validate no token mismatches surface after full rollout
Aisha: updating status page and sending targeted emails to top affected tenants. Will update support tickets with workaround steps
Maria: proposed postmortem owners — Jordan (detection & mitigation), Leo (root cause + long-term fix), Aisha (customer comms).
eng-sre: temporary mitigation plan: keep jwks_cache_ttl=600s until Okta status clears + one successful rotation window observed; then rollback and re-evaluate token verifier error handling
Leo: will escalate to Okta engineering if we don't see stable recovery within 60m. we'll also run token verification integrity checks (sample tokens) after rollback
incident-bot: NOTE: mitigation was config-only; no credential or key material was exposed per initial checks.
Jordan: leaving notes and handoff in the incident doc. thanks everyone.
Leo: will continue updates in-thread and in the incident doc. end of thread.
